key_points.text: In this episode, I speak with Gerald Rushden, senior member of the QIS structuring team at Laquiry Bank.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode, I speak with Gerald Rushden, senior member of the QIS structuring team at Laquiry Bank.

key_points.text: Our conversation largely revolves around commodity strategies, including thoughts on trend following, commodity carry, commodity congestion, and commodity volatility carry.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our conversation largely revolves around commodity strategies, including thoughts on trend following, commodity carry, commodity congestion, and commodity volatility carry.

key_points.text: Gerald argues that the latter three are particularly well suited to be paired with equity hedging strategies.
key_points.evidence_quote: Gerald argues that the latter three are particularly well suited to be paired with equity hedging strategies, and we spend quite a bit of time discussing the major design levers behind each approach.

thesis: The episode discusses the evolution of quantitative investment strategy (QIS) desks, noting that the industry has improved over the last decade due to greater sophistication, rigorous client analysis, and a shift away from blindly applying academic literature or porting equity quant strategies to macro assets. The conversation highlights that modern approaches are more open to ideas not derived from academic papers and acknowledge specific challenges in macro trading, such as fewer tradable instruments, higher correlations in rates, and vastly different volatility profiles across commodities.
